objective: Provide authoritative project master data and member-based data scope for the asset library and future business modules.
users: Project owners and project administrators maintaining projects and members
Project members and read-only members consuming project-scoped business data
Business modules resolving project summaries and access scope through a public contract

requirements.statement: Maintain a minimal tenant-scoped project directory with an immutable owner role and controlled member roles.
acceptance: Project codes are unique per tenant
Owner, administrator, member and read-only roles are validated server-side
requirements.source: User-confirmed design section 1 and project-scope decision
counterexample: Using frontend Mock projects as an authorization source
Allowing duplicate project codes within a tenant

requirements.statement: Expose stable project summary, membership and access-scope contracts without allowing consumers to read project tables.
acceptance: A consumer can resolve project status and current-user membership through public APIs
Cross-tenant and non-member access does not disclose project data
counterexample: A business module joins project private tables
The browser submits trusted membership conclusions

requirements.statement: Archived projects remain readable to authorized users but reject writes through all consuming modules.
acceptance: Archiving changes the project to read-only
Restoring re-enables writes according to the existing membership
counterexample: Archived projects still accept asset uploads or metadata changes

invariants: Effective authorization combines platform RBAC, project role scope and entity state
Project data is tenant scoped and project rows are not physically deleted
Business consumers use public contracts rather than project private tables
Project and membership writes are audited

selected_approach.name: Dedicated ccb-project business module
selected_approach.reason: It creates one authoritative project data owner and a reusable access contract without placing business rules in platform/system.

alternatives.name: Project catalog inside data migration
alternatives.rejected_because: It would duplicate project ownership for future business modules.

alternatives.name: Project data in platform/system
alternatives.rejected_because: It would mix business project ownership into the system administration platform.

components.name: Project application service
components.responsibility: Validate and coordinate project and member lifecycle

components.name: Project access contract
components.responsibility: Expose stable summaries and membership decisions to consumers

components.name: Project Context Store
components.responsibility: Expose the selected formal project to frontend business pages

interfaces.name: Project REST API
interfaces.contract: Authenticated project CRUD, membership and current-user scope

interfaces.name: Project context Java API
interfaces.contract: Tenant-scoped project summary and access decision

data_flows.output: Updated project summary or explicit rejection

error_handling.behavior: Return conflict without overwriting the newer state
error_handling.recovery: Reload the project and retry with the current version
Request membership through the authorized project process
Restore the project through an authorized action

verification_strategy.signal: Project and membership API results for each role and tenant
Archived projects reject writes and restored projects recover access
verification_strategy.method: State-transition API tests and consumer contract tests

assumptions.text: The initial project domain only needs the confirmed minimal directory
assumptions.falsifier: An approved requirement adds plans, milestones, budgets or risks

unknowns.question: What final module path and public package names will the module Owner approve?
unknowns.impact: Blocks ready status and implementation scope, but not the approved product design

decisions.decision: Use platform RBAC plus project member scope
decisions.reason: Separates operation permission from project data range

decisions.decision: Deliver a minimal project directory first
decisions.reason: Avoids expanding into complete project management

risks.risk: An unstable project contract affects every downstream module
risks.mitigation: Approve DTOs and role semantics before implementation and run consumer contract tests

approval.evidence: User confirmed all seven design sections and selected the dedicated-module approach.
